ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows a cumulative curve graph: the horizontal axis is labeled Demand (in KW), with a range approximately from 5,000 to 13,000 kW; the vertical axis is labeled Percent of days, with a range from 0 to 100. The curve rises as demand increases, and approaches 100% when near 13,000 kW. Find 12,000 kW on the horizontal axis, read upward to the cumulative curve, and the corresponding vertical-axis value is about 97%. Because this is a cumulative graph, 97% represents the proportion of days with demand less than or equal to 12,000 kW. The power plant capacity is 12,000 kW per day, and the situation in which demand cannot be met is when demand exceeds 12,000 kW, so the proportion is 100% - 97% = 3%.

raw_record.question_text: The cumulative graph gives the electricity demand of a certain town. The power plant that provides electricity to this town is capable of generating 12,000 kW daily. On what percent of days will the power plant not be able to meet the demand for electricity?

method.method_draft: First describe/read the graph: the x-axis is Demand in kW, the y-axis is Percent of days, and the curve is cumulative, rising toward 100%. From the text, identify the plant capacity as 12,000 kW and the requested event as days when demand exceeds that capacity. On the image, locate x = 12,000 kW, move up to the cumulative curve, and read the y-value, which is about 97%. Since a cumulative graph gives the percent of days with demand at or below that demand level, compute 100% - 97% ≈ 3%.
